name: Sir Garnet
summary: A Napoleon variant where a player can take a 5-card widow to force a bid of all five tricks for double stakes.
rules_text: Use a standard 52-card deck. Each player gets 5 cards dealt 3 then 2, and a 5-card widow is dealt face down. Starting left of dealer, each player in turn may take the widow: combine it with their hand to 10 cards, keep any 5 and discard 5 face down unseen, and they must then bid Nap, meaning they must win all 5 tricks, with double penalty if they fail. If no one takes it, conduct normal Nap bidding with lower bids allowed. The highest bidder leads first and that suit is trump and must be a trump. Play is standard trick-taking: must follow suit if able, otherwise may trump or discard. Highest card of led suit wins, beaten by highest trump if any. Winner leads next. Scoring is chip settlement: if bidder makes, each opponent pays them; if bidder fails, bidder pays each opponent, doubled when the widow was taken. No extra credit beyond making or breaking the bid.
rating_reason: Specific trick-taking bidding game with extra hand, strategic.
